verdict.rationale: Omarchy's own Install section of the Omarchy Menu is a first-party, curated way to install applications such as editors, terminals and development environments, and a user reports that installing software is easy and fast. However, the documented catalog is a short curated list, nowhere near thousands of applications. The 'thousands of community plugins' are plugins, not applications, and Arch package mirrors belong to the host platform, so neither is credited. Missing for 10: evidence of an official catalog with thousands of applications, documented catalog browsing/search, and independent corroboration of catalog breadth.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can install thousands of applications directly from an official software catalog

citations.quote: Neovim is the default, with VSCode, Cursor, Zed, Sublime Text, Helix, Vim, and Emacs ready to install.
Pick your preference under _Install > Terminal_ in the Omarchy menu.
Install Ruby on Rails, Laravel, Node.js, and a long list of other development environments from the Omarchy menu.
installing software is easy and lightning-fast
